title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 1
focusVi: Rèn luyện kỹ năng phát triển ý mạch lạc từ câu trả lời trực tiếp đến việc mở rộng bằng trải nghiệm cá nhân và lập luận đa chiều.

qs: Do you currently work or are you a student?
What made you choose this particular field?
What do you find most challenging about your daily tasks?
Do you plan to continue in this line of work or study in the future?
Where is your hometown located?
What do people in your hometown usually do for leisure?
Has your hometown changed much over the last ten years?
Would you say your hometown is a suitable place for young people to live?

part2.prompt: Describe a person who taught you a useful skill when you were younger.
bullets: who this person was
what skill they taught you
how they taught it to you
and explain why this skill has been useful in your life

part3: What qualities distinguish an exceptional teacher from an ordinary one?
Do you believe children learn practical skills better from parents or from school teachers?
How have online learning platforms transformed the way people acquire new practical skills?
Should traditional crafts still be taught to younger generations in modern society?
Why do some adults find it considerably harder to learn new skills than children do?

p1: Right now, I am working as a graphic designer at an advertising agency. I really enjoy the creative freedom it offers, especially when working on brand campaigns for local businesses.

I chose graphic design because I have always loved visual arts since childhood. Creating digital illustrations allows me to turn imaginative concepts into tangible products that actually solve communication problems.

The toughest part is definitely managing tight deadlines while maintaining high standards. For instance, when several clients request urgent revisions simultaneously, it demands intense concentration and rapid problem-solving under pressure.
Yes, I definitely intend to stay in this creative industry. Eventually, I hope to establish my own boutique design studio to mentor novice designers and handle independent projects.
My hometown is Da Nang, a vibrant coastal city in central Vietnam. It is situated right along the coast, offering stunning sandy beaches and iconic bridges that attract countless visitors.

Locals usually gather at beachside coffee shops or stroll along the Han River promenade in the evening. During weekends, families often organize seaside barbecues or go hiking around Son Tra Peninsula.

It has developed dramatically over the past decade. Modern skyscrapers, upgraded bridges, and international hospitality chains have transformed our quiet town into a bustling commercial hub with far better public amenities.

Yes, it offers a balanced lifestyle with reasonable living expenses and emerging job opportunities in tourism and tech. However, ambitious graduates seeking massive corporate environments might still prefer larger metropolitan cities.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about my grandfather, who taught me fundamental woodworking and basic carpentry when I was around twelve. He was a retired craftsman who spent most afternoons in his backyard workshop filled with aromatic sawdust and hand tools. Initially, he showed me how to measure precisely, saw timber safely, and assemble small wooden joints using chisels. Rather than simply lecturing, he had me build a simple birdhouse from scratch, guiding my hands patiently whenever I made an uneven cut. He always emphasized patience and precision over speed. That skill has proven remarkably useful throughout my adult life. On a practical level, I rarely need to hire repair technicians because I can easily assemble furniture, fix squeaky hinges, or repair damaged shelves myself, saving significant money. More importantly, this craft taught me resourcefulness and how to approach complex problems methodically. Whenever I feel overwhelmed by work, doing manual repairs serves as a grounding, therapeutic outlet. I am immensely grateful for his guidance, as it gave me practical self-reliance.
p3: In my view, an exceptional teacher possesses genuine empathy and adaptability, whereas an ordinary one merely delivers the curriculum. Great educators tailor their methods to individual learning styles, using relatable analogies when students struggle. For example, my high school chemistry teacher turned dry formulas into interactive experiments, igniting genuine curiosity. Ultimately, the ability to inspire lifelong curiosity rather than enforce rote memorization is what truly sets them apart.

I believe parents are better suited for teaching everyday life skills, while teachers excel at structured technical abilities. Parents offer daily, informal reinforcement in home environments, such as cooking meals or budgeting pocket money. In contrast, classroom settings are inherently constrained by rigid academic syllabuses. Therefore, while schools provide essential academic fundamentals, parents play a far more decisive role in cultivating practical, real-world autonomy.

Digital platforms have radically democratized skill acquisition by making specialized knowledge accessible on demand. Previously, mastering an instrument or coding required expensive private tutors, whereas now learners can pause and replay high-quality video tutorials anytime. However, online learning often lacks immediate personalized feedback, which can lead to bad habits. Overall, while self-discipline is essential, internet resources have certainly lowered the barriers to learning practical crafts.

Undoubtedly, preserving traditional crafts is vital because they embody cultural heritage and foster patience. In our fast-paced digital era, many young people only interact with mass-produced goods. Learning traditional skills like pottery or weaving connects youth with their ancestral identity while developing tangible motor skills. Consequently, integrating these crafts into school curricula ensures our unique cultural legacy survives alongside rapid technological advancements.

This difficulty primarily stems from psychological barriers and neuroplasticity rather than pure intellectual decline. Adults are often paralyzed by the fear of looking foolish, whereas children embrace trial and error without self-consciousness. Furthermore, adult responsibilities like careers and family drastically limit the focused practice time required for mastery. Thus, emotional inhibitions and time constraints make skill acquisition substantially more challenging for mature learners.

title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 2
focusVi: Rèn luyện kỹ năng so sánh quá khứ - hiện tại và phát triển lập luận đa chiều trong phần thảo luận.

qs: Do you live in a house or an apartment?
What is your favourite room in your home?
How long have you lived there?
Would you like to move to a different home in the future?
What is the busiest part of your day?
Do you usually follow the same routine every day?
Did you have a different daily routine when you were younger?
What would you like to change about your current routine?

part2.prompt: Describe a memorable place you visited that you would like to return to
bullets: where this place is
when and with whom you went there
what you did while you were there
and explain why you would like to visit this place again

part3: Why do some people prefer revisiting familiar holiday destinations rather than exploring new ones?
How has international travel changed compared to several decades ago?
Do you think excessive tourism can destroy the unique charm of historic destinations?
In what ways can local governments balance economic gains from tourism with environmental conservation?
Will virtual reality travel ever completely replace actual physical journeys?

p1: Currently, I live in a modest apartment on the tenth floor of a high-rise. I love it because it offers quiet surroundings and a fantastic panoramic view of the bustling city skyline below.
My bedroom is definitely my favourite space because it serves as my private sanctuary. I have set up a cosy reading corner by the window where I unwind with fiction novels every evening.
I have resided there for nearly four years now, ever since my family relocated for my university studies. It has truly become a familiar and welcoming home filled with warm personal memories.
Yes, eventually I would love to move into a suburban detached house with a spacious backyard garden. Having some greenery and fresh air would be ideal for hosting weekend barbecues with friends.
The morning rush between eight and ten is certainly my most hectic period. That is when I commute through heavy traffic and prepare my daily schedule before tackling demanding work assignments.
For the most part, yes, my weekdays follow a strict schedule to maintain productivity. However, on weekends I intentionally abandon set timetables so I can sleep in and catch up on personal hobbies.

Certainly, my childhood routine was far more relaxed and carefree. Back then, my primary responsibility was attending school, leaving plenty of free daylight hours to ride bicycles with neighbouring friends after classes.
I would definitely like to incorporate regular physical exercise into my morning hours. At the moment, I often skip workouts due to waking up late, which leaves me feeling sluggish by afternoon.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about Ninh Binh, a stunning province in northern Vietnam that left an indelible impression on me. I took a weekend trip there about two years ago with two of my closest university friends after finishing our final exams. During our three-day stay, we rented scooters to explore the tranquil countryside, marveling at the towering limestone karsts rising dramatically from emerald rice paddies. One of the highlights was taking a traditional wooden boat ride through Trang An, drifting quietly through mystical flooded caves and ancient temples nestled amidst towering cliffs. We also hiked up hundreds of stone steps to the peak of Mua Cave, which rewarded us with an awe-inspiring panoramic view of the valley below at sunset. The primary reason I am eager to return is its peaceful, untouched ambiance, which provided a much-needed respite from chaotic city life. Although it has gained popularity among international backpackers, many corners remain serene and authentic. Next time, I hope to stay for an entire week at a local homestay, simply reading books, cycling through misty valleys, and immersing myself in the local culture once again.
p3: In my opinion, people return to familiar spots primarily because it guarantees relaxation without unexpected stress. When visiting a known destination, travellers already understand the local transport, cuisine, and accommodation standards. In contrast, venturing into uncharted territory requires extensive planning and carries potential risks of disappointment. Therefore, those seeking pure comfort often gravitate towards places where fond memories are already established.

Undeniably, international tourism has become far more accessible and democratised than in the past. Decades ago, overseas holidays were exclusive luxury privileges reserved for affluent demographics. Today, budget airlines, online booking platforms, and digital navigation make global travel affordable and straightforward for ordinary citizens. As a result, cross-border journeys have transformed from rare once-in-a-lifetime adventures into routine annual leisure activities for millions worldwide.

Yes, uncontrolled overtourism can undoubtedly erode the cultural authenticity and heritage of historic towns. When sites are overwhelmed by massive tour groups, local shops frequently get replaced by generic souvenir stalls and international chains, stripping away regional identity. Venice and Hoi An exemplify how overcrowding can strain infrastructure and alienate native residents. Ultimately, unregulated commercialisation risks turning authentic communities into superficial tourist spectacles.

Authorities should enforce strict sustainability policies while using tourism revenues to finance ecological protection. Specifically, governments can impose daily visitor quotas on vulnerable sites and levy eco-taxes on visitors to subsidise conservation initiatives. For instance, Bhutan limits visitor arrivals through daily tariffs, safeguarding its fragile Himalayan ecosystem while ensuring high-value revenue. Consequently, such measured approaches guarantee steady economic income without sacrificing natural habitats.

Personally, I highly doubt virtual simulations will ever make physical travel obsolete. While advanced VR technology offers remarkable 3D visuals and immersive walkthroughs of distant landmarks, it cannot replicate tangible sensory experiences such as tasting local street food, feeling sea breezes, or connecting warmly with hospitable locals. Thus, virtual reality will remain a convenient supplementary preview rather than a genuine substitute for real-world exploration.

title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 3
focusVi: Luyện tập kỹ năng mở rộng câu trả lời tự nhiên, cấu trúc bài nói mạch lạc và phân tích đa chiều về tác động của công nghệ.

qs: What kinds of food do you enjoy eating the most?
Do you prefer eating at home or dining out?
Did you learn how to cook when you were younger?
Is it important for children to learn basic cooking skills?
How often do you spend time with your close friends?
What qualities do you value most in a good friend?
Do you prefer having many casual acquaintances or a few close friends?
Has your friendship circle changed much since childhood?

part2.prompt: Describe a piece of technology you find useful in your daily life
bullets: what device or application it is
how long you have been using it
what you mainly use it for
and explain why you find it so useful to you.

part3: How has modern technology changed the way people communicate with each other?
Do you think older generations face significant difficulties in adapting to new technologies?
To what extent has the reliance on smart devices affected people's cognitive abilities or memory?
What impact might artificial intelligence have on future employment opportunities?
Should governments establish stricter regulations on data privacy and technological surveillance?

p1: I'm a massive fan of traditional home-cooked meals, especially noodle soups like pho. They are nutritious and comforting, and I usually have a bowl at my local eatery every weekend.

I definitely prefer home-cooked food because it's much healthier and cost-effective. Even though dining out saves time during busy weekdays, preparing dinner at home gives me total control over ingredients.
Yes, my mother taught me basic kitchen skills around age ten. I started by boiling rice and frying eggs, which really helped me become self-reliant when I went to college.

Absolutely, cooking is an essential life skill rather than just a chore. Learning simple recipes early fosters independence and helps youngsters make healthier dietary choices instead of relying on fast food.
I catch up with my closest mates at least once a week. We usually hang out at a quiet café on Sunday afternoons to unwind and chat about our daily routines.
For me, genuine loyalty and honesty matter the most. A true friend should be someone who offers sincere advice rather than empty flattery, especially when you face difficult challenges in life.
I much prefer having a tight-knit circle of three or four trustworthy friends. Broad networks are nice for networking, but deep emotional connections require genuine time and energy to maintain.
Quite significantly, to be honest. While I lost touch with most of my primary school peers due to relocating, I've developed deeper, lasting bonds with friends made during university.
answers.sample: I'd like to talk about an electronic tablet that has become completely indispensable in my everyday life, namely the iPad Air with a stylus pen. I bought this device about two years ago when I started my master's degree, and since then, it has virtually replaced all my paper notebooks. Primarily, I utilize it for annotating digital documents, organizing study schedules, and reading academic journals. Whenever I attend seminars or lectures, I can quickly jot down handwritten notes directly onto PDFs without printing hundreds of sheets. Aside from academic work, I also rely on it for video editing and catching up on educational podcasts in the evening. What makes this piece of technology so remarkably useful to me is its seamless portability combined with incredible efficiency. Instead of lugging around heavy binders, everything I need is synchronized across cloud storage. Furthermore, the ability to search through handwritten text saves me immense time during revision periods. Ultimately, it has streamlined both my productivity and workflow, making learning far more engaging and organized than ever before.
p3: Modern technology has undeniably accelerated interpersonal communication by making it instantaneous regardless of geographical distances. Platforms like messaging apps enable instant sharing of thoughts and media. However, this convenience often comes at the cost of genuine emotional depth, as text messages cannot fully convey tone or body language. Consequently, while our connectivity has expanded exponentially, the intimacy of face-to-face dialogue has somewhat diminished.

In my view, many seniors do struggle with contemporary devices due to rapid interface changes and steep learning curves. While young digital natives grasp intuitive gestures effortlessly, older individuals frequently worry about making irreversible technical mistakes or falling victim to online scams. Therefore, designing more accessible user interfaces and offering community digital literacy programs are crucial steps to prevent their marginalization.

Excessive dependence on smart gadgets has noticeably weakened our ability to retain information independently. Since algorithms and search engines store contacts and solve queries instantly, people rarely exercise their memory. For instance, hardly anyone remembers phone numbers today compared to a couple of decades ago. While this frees up mental bandwidth for complex tasks, it undeniably makes everyday recall significantly lazier.

Artificial intelligence will undoubtedly disrupt the job market by automating routine analytical and clerical duties. Traditional roles in data entry or basic customer support may disappear completely. Nonetheless, this transformation will likely create fresh demand for professionals who can oversee, refine, and ethically manage these automated systems. Thus, workers must continually reskill to remain competitive rather than fear complete obsolescence.

I firmly believe stricter legal frameworks are urgent to curb unchecked data harvesting by tech conglomerates. Without rigorous oversight, personal information is routinely commercialized or exploited for targeted manipulation without informed consent. Although tech companies often argue that heavy regulation stifles digital innovation, safeguarding citizen privacy must take precedence. Hence, robust legislation like strict privacy laws is essential for maintaining democratic trust.

title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 4
focusVi: Rèn luyện kỹ năng kết hợp tự sự với đánh giá cá nhân và phát triển luận điểm trừu tượng trong phần thảo luận.

qs: Do you frequently take part in physical activities?
What kind of sports are most popular among young people in your country?
Did you enjoy physical education classes when you were in school?
Do you prefer exercising alone or working out with others?
What kind of weather do you enjoy the most?
Does the climate in your area change dramatically throughout the year?
How does bad weather usually affect your daily routine?
Do you regularly check the weather forecast before heading out?

part2.prompt: Describe a book or film that had a strong influence on your thinking
bullets: what the title of the book or film was
when and where you first read or watched it
what key themes or message it explored
and explain why it had such a lasting impact on you

part3: How do films and literature shape societal values over time?
Do you think reading books offers deeper intellectual benefits than watching cinema?
Why do some stories maintain their relevance across multiple generations?
Should filmmakers and authors feel an ethical responsibility toward younger audiences?
In what ways has digital media changed how people consume written and visual narratives?

p1: Honestly, I try to stay active by jogging three times a week around my local lake. It helps relieve academic stress and keeps my stamina up after long hours of sitting at a desk.
Football is indisputably the top choice here. You can see teenagers kicking balls on almost every street corner or turf pitch every weekend because it's both social and affordable.
Not really, to be honest. Our classes were overly rigid and focused heavily on repetitive drills like shuttle runs, rather than letting us play engaging team sports like badminton or basketball.
I definitely lean towards solo sessions. Working out alone at the gym lets me listen to my favourite podcasts and progress at my own pace without having to coordinate schedules with friends.
I'm particularly fond of crisp, overcast mornings. The mild temperature makes it pleasant to walk outside without breaking into a sweat, especially during the transitional weeks of autumn.
Yes, quite substantially. Where I live, summers are scorching and humid with sudden downpours, while winters turn remarkably chilly and dry, requiring heavy jackets and heaters.
Heavy rain invariably disrupts my commute. Flooded streets slow traffic to a crawl, so I usually postpone non-essential outdoor errands and switch to working from home instead.
Yes, it has become second nature. I glance at a weather app every morning to decide whether I need to pack an umbrella or pick lightweight clothing for the day.
answers.sample: I'd like to talk about a film that genuinely reshaped my worldview, which is the biographical drama 'The Pursuit of Happyness'. I first watched it during my senior year of high school on a quiet Sunday afternoon at home, at a time when I was feeling quite anxious about upcoming university entrance exams. The narrative centres around Chris Gardner, a struggling salesman in San Francisco who faces severe financial hardship and eventual homelessness while raising his young son. At its core, the movie explores resilience, paternal devotion, and the unyielding pursuit of dignity against overwhelming odds. What made this film so profoundly impactful for me was its sheer authenticity. Unlike typical Hollywood success stories, it didn't sugarcoat the painful reality of failure and emotional exhaustion. Watching the protagonist endure relentless setbacks without surrendering his integrity made me realize that perseverance isn't merely about working hard; it's about staying composed when everything seems stacked against you. Whenever I encounter professional obstacles today, remembering Gardner's resolve gives me the psychological fortitude to keep pushing forward.
p3: In my view, creative works act as a mirror that both reflects and guides public consciousness. When stories portray marginalized groups with nuance or highlight pressing ethical dilemmas, they prompt viewers to reassess ingrained prejudices. For instance, films addressing mental health have substantially reduced social stigma in recent years. Thus, art often precedes broader cultural shifts by humanizing complex issues.

I believe written texts generally foster deeper analytical thinking. Reading demands active cognitive involvement because individuals must visualize characters, interpret subtext, and construct entire worlds mentally. Conversely, cinema spoon-feeds sensory details through imagery and sound design, which can make viewing a relatively passive affair. Therefore, while both stimulate creativity, literature cultivates superior concentration and imaginative depth.

Timeless stories invariably address universal human conditions rather than fleeting social trends. Masterpieces explore enduring motifs like love, ambition, mortality, and justice, which resonate regardless of historical context. For example, Shakespearean plays like 'Macbeth' remain compelling today because the pitfalls of unchecked ambition are just as relevant in modern corporate culture. Ultimately, stories survive when their core moral truths transcend temporal boundaries.

Without a doubt, creators targeting impressionable audiences bear a substantial moral duty. Children and teenagers naturally emulate the behaviors, language, and moral compasses showcased by fictional protagonists. If media glamorizes antisocial behavior without presenting the accompanying consequences, it can distort youthful perceptions. Therefore, storytellers should strive to entertain while embedding constructive ethical frameworks that foster empathy rather than cynicism.

Digital platforms have fundamentally shortened attention spans and fragmented how we consume narratives. People now gravitate toward bite-sized video clips or serialized streaming episodes rather than lengthy novels or epic cinema. While this provides unprecedented convenience and accessibility, it often diminishes our patience for slow-paced, reflective storytelling. Consequently, contemporary narrative consumption has prioritized immediate gratification over immersive, contemplative engagement.

title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 5
focusVi: Luyện tập kỹ năng kể chuyện có cấu trúc rõ ràng và phát triển lập luận đa chiều về trách nhiệm cộng đồng.

qs: How do you usually travel to work or study?
Do you prefer using public transport or private vehicles?
Has the transport system in your hometown changed much recently?
Do you think traffic congestion will be solved in the future?
Do you enjoy going shopping for clothes?
Where do you usually go when you want to buy groceries?
Do you prefer shopping online or in traditional stores?
Have your shopping habits changed compared to the past?

part2.prompt: Describe a time you helped someone with an important task
bullets: who this person was and what they needed
when and where you offered your assistance
how you helped them complete the task
and explain why your help was meaningful to both of you

part3: Why do some people hesitate to help strangers in public situations?
Do you think children should be taught to do volunteer work from an early age?
Should governments rely on charitable organizations to solve social welfare issues?
How has modern technology changed the way people offer and receive help?
In what ways can helping others contribute to a person's psychological well-being?

p1: I usually commute to university by motorbike because it is the most flexible option. Navigating narrow alleyways in Hanoi is much faster this way, especially during the chaotic morning rush hour.

I definitely lean towards private vehicles like scooters. Although public buses are cheaper and eco-friendly, my motorbike allows me to take spontaneous detours without waiting at crowded bus stops in hot weather.

Yes, it has improved significantly over the past few years. The city has introduced elevated metro lines and widened several arterial roads, which has eased traffic bottlenecks considerably during peak times.

I am cautiously optimistic. With upcoming investments in smart traffic management and modern mass transit systems like sky trains, gridlocks should decrease, though rapid urbanization might slow down that progress.
To be honest, not really because finding the right fit can be exhausting. I only browse boutique stores when I urgently need something specific, such as a formal blazer for a presentation.

I typically head to the wet market near my neighborhood every weekend. The leafy vegetables and fish are remarkably fresher there compared to supermarkets, and I can negotiate prices directly with local vendors.

I favor e-commerce platforms like Shopee because of convenience and competitive pricing. I can compare customer reviews and buy electronic accessories in just a few clicks instead of traveling across town.

Certainly. In the past, I bought clothes impulsively based on fleeting trends. Nowadays, I am far more budget-conscious, prioritizing durable staples and waiting for seasonal discounts before making any major purchase.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about a time I assisted my elderly neighbor, Mr. Binh, in setting up a smartphone to connect with his family overseas. This happened around six months ago during the pandemic restrictions when he felt quite isolated. Mr. Binh had just received an iPhone from his daughter living in Australia, but being unfamiliar with modern technology, he was completely overwhelmed by the touchscreen and apps. Seeing his struggle, I offered to visit his apartment over the weekend. I spent several hours patiently installing messaging apps, configuring large fonts, and creating a step-by-step notebook with hand-drawn diagrams so he could practice independently. To make sure he was comfortable, I also simulated video calls with him across the room until he mastered answering and muting. When he successfully connected with his young grandson in Sydney for the first time, tears came to his eyes. Witnessing his sheer joy was incredibly heartwarming. It made me realize how a small investment of my time could bridge an enormous emotional distance and alleviate someone's loneliness.
p3: In my view, bystander apathy and fear of liability are the primary deterrents. Many people worry about falling victim to scams or being wrongfully blamed if medical emergencies worsen. For instance, in fast-paced cities, commuters often assume someone else will intervene, so nobody acts. Consequently, self-preservation frequently outweighs altruistic instincts in crowded public environments.

I strongly believe community service should be embedded into early schooling. Engaging in charity fosters empathy and civic responsibility, helping young learners look beyond their personal bubbles. Unlike passive classroom lectures on ethics, cleaning a neighborhood park or distributing food gives children hands-on experience with social inequality. Ultimately, early exposure creates more compassionate and proactive future citizens.

From my perspective, charities should supplement rather than replace official social safety nets. While non-profits can mobilize rapid grassroots relief during crises like floods, only state authorities possess the resources and legislative mandate to tackle systemic poverty. Over-relying on voluntary philanthropy makes vulnerable groups susceptible to funding fluctuations. Therefore, governments must bear core welfare duties permanently.

Digital innovations have revolutionized philanthropy by eliminating geographical boundaries. Online crowdfunding campaigns and mobile micro-donations allow anyone to transfer funds instantly to disaster victims across the globe. By contrast, traditional assistance required physical presence or cumbersome banking procedures. This hyper-connectivity dramatically accelerates humanitarian interventions, making support far more immediate and democratic than ever before.

Assisting others triggers what psychologists call a 'helper's high', which releases endorphins and reduces stress hormones. When individuals alleviate someone else's burden, they experience heightened self-worth and purpose, buffering against loneliness. Unlike solitary achievements that yield short-lived satisfaction, fostering reciprocal human bonds builds long-term mental resilience. Hence, prosocial behavior directly nurtures personal happiness and emotional stability.

title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 6
focusVi: Luyện tập cách phát triển ý bằng phương pháp đưa ra lý do và ví dụ thực tế, cùng khả năng thảo luận các khía cạnh xã hội trừu tượng.

qs: What kind of music do you usually listen to when you want to relax?
Did you learn to play any musical instrument during your childhood?
Do you prefer listening to recorded songs at home or attending live concerts?
Do you think people's taste in music changes as they get older?
Do you enjoy reading books or articles in your free time?
Did you read many storybooks when you were a young child?
Do you prefer reading printed paper books or using electronic screens?
What types of books do you find most difficult or boring to read?

part2.prompt: Describe a practical skill you would like to learn in the future
bullets: what skill it is
how you would learn it
who you could learn it from or practice with
and explain why you want to acquire this particular skill

part3: Which skills do you consider essential for young people entering the workforce nowadays?
Do you believe traditional craft skills are losing their value in modern industrialized society?
To what extent can online platforms and tutorials replace formal classroom instruction?
Why do some mature adults find it harder to acquire new skills compared to children?
Should governments invest more public funding into adult retraining programs?

p1: I usually turn to acoustic indie folk because its gentle melodies soothe my mind after hectic study sessions. For instance, listening to soft guitar tracks helps me unwind and fall asleep much faster at night.

Yes, my parents enrolled me in piano classes when I was eight. Although practicing repetitive scales was quite tedious back then, playing simple classical pieces gave me a solid appreciation for musical rhythm.

I definitely prefer listening at home with noise-canceling headphones. Live concerts are often overwhelming and overpriced, whereas streaming at home allows me to enjoy my favorite playlists in peaceful comfort anytime.

Certainly, our musical preferences evolve alongside our life stages. Teenagers often crave energetic pop or hip-hop, while older individuals, like my parents, tend to gravitate toward nostalgic acoustic ballads and classical compositions.

Yes, I read self-help articles and non-fiction books almost every evening. Reading broadens my perspective on personal growth and gives me practical tips that I can immediately apply in my daily life.

Absolutely, I was fascinated by illustrated fairy tales and folklore during primary school. My mother used to read me bedtime stories every night, which sparked my imagination and nurtured my lifelong reading habit.

I still lean towards printed books because turning physical pages feels tactile and causes less eye strain. Staring at backlit screens all day for work already exhausts my eyes, making physical books a relief.

I find dense academic textbooks on economics particularly dry and tedious. The abundance of jargon and abstract formulas makes them struggle to retain my attention, unlike engaging narrative non-fiction or biographies.
answers.sample: If I had the opportunity to master a new skill, I would definitely choose culinary arts, specifically cooking authentic Southeast Asian and Mediterranean dishes. To achieve this, I would start by enrolling in an intensive weekend cooking workshop at a local culinary academy. Alongside structured classes, I would supplement my training by following instructional video courses by renowned chefs and practicing fundamental knife techniques and seasoning methods at home. I would love to learn directly from an experienced chef, but on a daily basis, I would practice alongside my grandmother, who is an extraordinary home cook with decades of traditional kitchen wisdom. Collaborating with her would make the journey much more meaningful. I really want to develop this ability for two main reasons. Firstly, cooking wholesome, balanced meals from scratch would dramatically improve my physical health and dietary habits. More importantly, food brings people together. Being able to prepare sophisticated feasts would allow me to host memorable weekend gatherings for my family and close friends, creating warm memories around delicious shared meals.
p3: In my view, digital literacy combined with adaptability is paramount in the modern job market. Technological tools evolve at breakneck speed, so employees must quickly master automated systems and artificial intelligence. While technical expertise matters, individuals lacking soft skills like emotional intelligence and creative problem-solving often struggle to collaborate effectively. Therefore, possessing a versatile blend of tech competence and interpersonal skills ensures long-term career resilience.

Not necessarily. Although automated manufacturing has replaced mass artisan production, handcrafted items have actually gained prestige as luxury goods. Consumers are increasingly willing to pay a premium for bespoke pottery, handwoven textiles, and woodwork because machine-made alternatives lack individuality and cultural heritage. Hence, while their economic utility on an industrial scale has diminished, traditional artisanal craftsmanship holds immense cultural and artistic significance today.

Online tutorials can supplement theoretical understanding, but they cannot entirely substitute structured classrooms. Digital learning offers tremendous flexibility and access to global expertise at low cost. However, it noticeably lacks hands-on supervision, immediate teacher feedback, and spontaneous peer discussions, which are vital for practical vocations like medicine or mechanics. Consequently, online platforms remain powerful complementary resources rather than total replacements for immersive institutional education.

I believe cognitive neuroplasticity and psychological barriers play major roles. Children absorb languages and motor patterns instinctively without fear of embarrassment. In contrast, adults often possess ingrained habits and suffer from performance anxiety, fearing failure when stepping outside their comfort zones. Furthermore, heavy occupational and domestic responsibilities leave mature learners with limited energy and time. Thus, psychological inhibitions and lifestyle constraints make adult learning significantly more challenging.

Without doubt, state investment in lifelong adult education is an economic necessity. Rapid automation and digital transformation threaten to render millions of conventional jobs obsolete. While private corporations rarely subsidize comprehensive reskilling for displaced workers, government-sponsored programs can bridge workforce skill gaps and reduce long-term unemployment expenditure. Ultimately, funding adult retraining safeguards national economic productivity and fosters greater social stability amidst rapid industrial disruption.

title: IELTS Speaking Mock Test 7
focusVi: Phát triển kỹ năng miêu tả trải nghiệm cá nhân mạch lạc và mở rộng quan điểm xã hội về văn hóa ẩm thực.

qs: What piece of technology do you use most often in your daily life?

answers.sample: One of the most unforgettable meals I have ever shared took place last autumn when my family gathered to celebrate my grandmother's eightieth birthday. The gathering brought together three generations, including my aunts, uncles, and cousins whom I hadn't seen in months. The atmosphere was incredibly lively and full of laughter from the moment we sat down. We ordered an array of local delicacies, such as grilled tiger prawns with chili salt, steamed squid, and a rich, fragrant seafood hotpot brimming with fresh herbs and vegetables. The freshness of the catch combined with traditional dipping sauces made every bite an absolute treat. What made this feast truly memorable was not just the delicious fare, but the overwhelming sense of togetherness. Seeing my grandmother beam with happiness as we toasted her health made me realize the profound value of family ties. In our fast-paced lives, having everyone together without digital distractions felt truly priceless, making it a meal I will cherish for years to come.
p3: Sharing food has always held deep symbolic value across cultures because it fosters bonding and hospitality. When people celebrate milestones, dining together creates a relaxed environment where participants can converse and express appreciation. While casual gifts are quickly forgotten, a celebratory feast provides shared sensory memories that deepen relationships. Ultimately, communal dining reinforces our social bonds during meaningful transitions.

In previous decades, families consistently gathered around the dinner table to share freshly cooked, wholesome meals. Nowadays, due to demanding work schedules and the rise of food delivery platforms, individual and fast-food dining have become commonplace. Although this shift brings convenience to busy professionals, it often diminishes household communication and leads to poor nutritional choices. Therefore, modern eating habits are considerably less communal and balanced.

To some extent, global fast-food franchises do challenge domestic eateries by dominating commercial areas and appealing strongly to younger consumers. However, traditional street food vendors still retain a loyal customer base because their recipes offer authentic local flavors at reasonable prices. While global chains provide consistency and speed, they rarely replicate the cultural heritage found in regional dishes, ensuring traditional gastronomy endures.

I firmly believe educational institutions should actively teach balanced eating habits. While parents hold primary responsibility for their children's diet, schools can provide structured knowledge on balanced nutrition and the health risks of processed foods. In contrast to unsupervised snacking at home, school-based programs establish lifelong healthy routines. Consequently, incorporating dietary education into the curriculum is essential for combating childhood obesity.

Culinary traditions are undeniably central to national identity as they reflect a country's climate, agricultural history, and social philosophy. For instance, Vietnam's emphasis on fresh herbs and shared communal bowls represents an agrarian lifestyle and community values. While globalization encourages culinary cross-pollination, authentic native dishes remain powerful cultural emblems. Thus, culinary heritage serves as a vital bridge preserving a country's distinct heritage.

answers.sample: I'd like to share an important decision I made about three years ago, which was switching my university major from accounting to graphic design. I had always possessed a creative flair, constantly doodling and designing posters for student clubs in my spare time. The dilemma was excruciating because accounting offered clear job security, and my parents strongly favoured that conventional path. I briefly considered finishing my degree first and pursuing art as a hobby, or perhaps doing a double major. However, I knew that splitting my energy would lead to mediocrity in both fields. After several heart-to-heart talks with my mentors, I took a leap of faith and transferred to design school. It proved to be a pivotal turning point in my life. Not only did I rediscover my genuine enthusiasm for learning, but it also opened doors to a fulfilling career in digital branding. Making that bold choice taught me that trusting one's instincts often outweighs simply playing it safe.
p3: Young adults usually encounter critical choices regarding their tertiary education, career direction, and financial independence. For instance, choosing whether to move out of the family home or rent an apartment requires weighing budget against autonomy. These choices are pivotal because they set the trajectory for their adulthood, forcing them to transition from parental reliance to personal accountability.

I believe a balanced synthesis of both is ideal. Pure logic provides rational risk assessment, such as evaluating financial returns when purchasing property, whereas intuition reflects our core values and emotional comfort. Relying solely on cold data might lead to technically sound but emotionally unsatisfying outcomes, so instinct should ultimately validate what logic proposes.

This indecisiveness often stems from analysis paralysis or fear of regret. In our modern consumer society, people are inundated with endless options, whether selecting a restaurant or buying a gadget. While having choices sounds positive, overthinking minor details drains mental energy, causing individuals to second-guess themselves over inconsequential outcomes.

The internet has democratised information, allowing consumers to compare reviews, prices, and professional advice before deciding. For example, people rarely book vacations or medical treatments without reading testimonials first. However, this abundance can also spread misinformation and cause cognitive overload, making the decision process far more complicated than in pre-digital times.

Parents should act as supportive advisers rather than authoritative decision-makers. While parental wisdom and life experience offer valuable perspectives on market stability, forcing a career upon a child often breeds resentment and poor performance. answers.sample: I would like to talk about the Hanoi Opera House, an exquisite historic building situated right in the heart of the capital. Constructed during the French colonial era, it stands out with its neoclassical architecture, featuring pale yellow facades, grand arched windows, and a striking black slate roof. Inside, the auditorium is breathtaking, adorned with velvet upholstery, crystal chandeliers, and ornate gilded ceilings, creating an aura of timeless elegance. The venue serves primarily as a premier cultural hub for classical concerts, ballet performances, and major national ceremonies. I have had the privilege of attending a symphony performance there, and the acoustic quality was simply phenomenal. What captivates me most about this building is how harmoniously it blends historical nostalgia with living culture. Unlike modern concrete skyscrapers that often feel sterile and identical, this monument has genuine character and soul. Standing in front of it transports you back in time, yet inside it continues to inspire modern audiences. It remains a proud landmark that reflects our city's multifaceted history, which is why it holds such a special place in my heart.
p3: In my view, traditional architecture prioritizes craftsmanship and cultural symbolism, often using natural materials like timber, stone, and decorative carvings that reflect local heritage. In contrast, modern architecture emphasizes minimalism, functional efficiency, and innovative industrial materials such as tempered glass and reinforced concrete. While modern designs maximize space and energy performance, traditional buildings evoke a profound sense of cultural identity that sleek contemporary skyscrapers often lack.

I strongly believe governments should invest in preserving historic structures because they embody a nation's collective memory and cultural heritage. Demolishing them for commercial developments permanently erases tangible history. For example, conserving ancient temples or colonial landmarks attracts cultural tourism and fosters civic pride. Although restoration can be costly, the long-term educational, cultural, and economic benefits far outweigh the financial expenditure, making public funding completely justifiable.

Architectural design profoundly influences physical and psychological wellbeing. Buildings with ample natural light, proper ventilation, and green spaces significantly lower stress levels and boost productivity. Conversely, cramped, windowless environments with poor air circulation can trigger fatigue and depression, as commonly observed in dense office cubicles. Ultimately, human-centric design is crucial because our immediate built surroundings directly dictate our mood, daily comfort, and long-term mental health.

To a large extent, vertical living is the most practical solution for densely populated megacities facing severe land scarcity. High-rise developments accommodate thousands of residents on relatively small footprints, curbing urban sprawl. However, without adequate accompanying infrastructure like public transit, green parks, and waste management, towering residential blocks can worsen congestion and foster social isolation. Therefore, high-rises are only sustainable when integrated into holistic urban planning.

I anticipate future architecture will pivot heavily towards ecological sustainability and smart technology. Architects will likely integrate living biophilic facades, solar harvesting glass, and automated energy management systems directly into structural designs to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. Rather than merely constructing aesthetic marvels, future builders will prioritize regenerative structures that actively purify air, conserve water, and coexist harmoniously with the surrounding natural ecosystem.

p3: In my view, hyper-competitiveness in the modern job market drives this trend. With instant messaging and email alerts on smartphones, employees are expected to respond around the clock. Chronic imbalance between career and personal life leads to severe physical burnout, emotional fatigue, and clinical anxiety. On a personal level, neglected relationships often dissolve because family members feel ignored or unsupported. Professionally, exhausted workers experience declining productivity and impaired decision-making. Therefore, neglecting equilibrium ultimately damages both individual well-being and organizational performance in the long term.

Children need quiet time simply to daydream, explore their surroundings, and develop emotional resilience organically.

I foresee a major shift toward flexible, output-oriented working arrangements rather than rigid office hours. With artificial intelligence handling repetitive tasks, four-day workweeks and asynchronous collaboration will likely become standard practice. Companies that enforce inflexible schedules will struggle to attract top talent. Ultimately, workplace success will be judged by actual output and creative impact, fostering healthier autonomy for professional employees.

The gift was a vintage-style scrapbook filled with carefully restored photographs spanning six decades of her life. It included black-and-white snapshots of her youth, images from her wedding, and candid moments with her grandchildren. To assemble it, I spent weeks discreetly gathering old negatives from my relatives, restoring them digitally, and printing them on archival matte paper. Alongside each photo, I handwrote brief anecdotes and favorite memories narrated by family members. When she unwrapped it, she was visibly moved to tears. This gift was extraordinarily meaningful because it brought back cherished memories from her past, some of which she hadn't seen in decades. Moreover, for me, creating it was a rare opportunity to connect deeply with my family heritage and demonstrate genuine gratitude for her lifelong guidance.

Many people favor experiential gifts, like concert tickets or weekend getaways, because tangible possessions eventually depreciate or become clutter. For example, traveling with a partner fosters enduring connection far more effectively than receiving expensive jewelry. In my view, regifting or returning an unsuitable item is entirely practical, provided it is handled discreetly. Technology will likely make gift-giving increasingly digital, automated, and personalized. While this eliminates guesswork and logistical hurdles, it might also diminish the spontaneous human warmth historically associated with selecting gifts.

answers.sample: I'd like to talk about the ancient town of Hoi An, an exceptionally well-preserved trading port located in central Vietnam that dates back to the fifteenth century. Visually, the town is absolutely stunning. It features narrow pedestrian streets lined with weathered yellow shophouses, ornate wooden Chinese assembly halls, and the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge. At dusk, hundreds of colourful silk lanterns illuminate the riverbanks, casting a magical glow over the water. When I visited last autumn, I spent hours strolling through the alleyways, admiring the centuries-old timber architecture and exploring traditional tea houses. I also took a wooden boat ride along the Thu Bon River during the lantern festival, releasing a small floating candle onto the water. What impressed me most was how seamlessly history blends with daily life there. Unlike sterile open-air museums, Hoi An is still vibrant with local residents living, cooking, and running traditional craft workshops in these ancient buildings. Experiencing such living history and tangible cultural preservation made a profound and lasting impression on me.
p3: In my view, safeguarding historical sites is crucial because they serve as tangible anchors to a nation's cultural identity. These monuments teach citizens about their architectural and social roots. Without adequate state preservation, commercial development would quickly replace irreplaceable heritage with modern high-rises. Therefore, public funding is essential to maintain this vital connection across generations.

Mass tourism often poses severe threats to structural integrity and local environments. Overcrowding can accelerate physical erosion of fragile masonry, and careless visitors might leave litter or graffiti. For instance, excessive foot traffic at ancient temples frequently causes irreversible foundation wear. Thus, unregulated visitor numbers can degrade the very attractions people come to admire.

I strongly believe schools should prioritize educational excursions to historic sites. Reading textbooks can feel dry, but standing inside a centuries-old fortress makes historical narratives tangible and engaging for young learners. While virtual resources are convenient, they cannot replicate the sensory impact of experiencing authentic artefacts in person. Hence, field trips offer unmatched educational value.

Charging reasonable admission fees is justifiable, provided the revenue directly funds conservation and site maintenance. Restoring ancient structures demands skilled craftsmen and expensive materials that municipal budgets cannot always cover. In contrast, making entry entirely free often leads to underfunded facilities and faster degradation. Consequently, modest fees strike the right balance between accessibility and preservation.

Emerging technologies like virtual reality and 3D reconstructions will fundamentally revolutionize historical engagement. Users will be able to step inside accurately restored digital replicas of ruined monuments from their own living rooms, making history globally accessible. While physical visits remain special, digital exhibits can protect vulnerable sites from foot traffic. Ultimately, technology will democratize and preserve our heritage.

answers.sample: I would like to talk about my maternal grandfather, a retired high school literature teacher whom I deeply respect and look up to. Unfortunately, contemporary society often appears to prioritize tangible accomplishments over ethical standards. The corporate world and social media frequently celebrate rapid financial success and status symbols, sometimes overlooking ethical compromises behind them. However, when prominent figures fall from grace due to scandals, public backlash quickly proves that integrity still matters deeply. Therefore, while achievement grabs headlines, genuine long-term respect still hinges on moral character.

Adolescents are often captivated by charismatic performers or wealthy influencers because of surface-level appeal. Integrity and humility are paramount. When well-known figures use their influential platform to advocate for social causes, such as charity work or climate action, they inspire fans constructively.
No, I value my personal privacy too much. Being constantly scrutinized by media cameras and online commentators sounds thoroughly exhausting, so I prefer leading a quiet, normal life.

Definitely. Despite their public careers, famous individuals are still human beings entitled to boundaries. Relentless paparazzi intrusion into someone's family life is unethical and should never be normalized.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about an artisanal bakery called The Daily Crust, located in a quiet alley near my neighborhood in Hanoi. It specializes in freshly baked sourdough bread, organic pastries, and specialty roasted coffee. I first stumbled upon this shop two years ago while taking an alternative shortcut home from university. The irresistible aroma of warm cinnamon rolls immediately drew me inside, and I have been a loyal patron ever since. What makes this small enterprise exceptionally successful is its uncompromising dedication to quality and personalized customer care. Unlike commercial industrial bakeries that rely on artificial preservatives, the owner sources organic whole grains from local farmers and ferments the dough naturally for twenty-four hours. Furthermore, the staff genuinely remember regular customers by name and often offer complimentary cookie samples to newcomers. Through word-of-mouth recommendations and clever Instagram marketing, the bakery has cultivated a devoted following. Even during economic downturns, people queue up every morning because the business delivers consistent culinary excellence alongside a warm, welcoming community atmosphere.
p3: Small retailers primarily struggle with economies of scale. Major supermarket chains purchase inventory in massive bulk, enabling them to offer aggressive discounts that independent shops cannot match. Additionally, multinational corporations possess expansive marketing budgets and sophisticated distribution networks. Consequently, independent shopkeepers must focus on distinctive craftsmanship and tailored service to survive, as engaging in a straightforward price war is virtually impossible.

Small enterprises serve as vital economic and social anchors. Financially, they generate neighborhood employment and keep monetary circulation within the domestic area rather than siphoning profits to overseas shareholders. Socially, these family-run businesses foster interpersonal connections, creating familiar gathering spaces where neighbors converse regularly. Therefore, they preserve unique neighborhood character and strengthen community cohesion far more effectively than faceless corporate outlets.

Yes, public investment in fledgling business founders is crucial. Young innovators frequently possess groundbreaking commercial concepts yet lack adequate collateral to secure conventional commercial bank loans. By offering seed funding, low-interest microloans, or subsidized incubation spaces, governments can mitigate early financial vulnerability. Although some start-ups inevitably fail, the successful ventures drive regional innovation, create jobs, and stimulate long-term economic growth.

Digital commerce has forced physical storefronts to shift from mere transaction hubs to experiential destinations. Instead of simply stocking shelves, successful retail stores now host interactive workshops, provide product demonstrations, and curate immersive aesthetic environments. Moreover, many have adopted hybrid omnichannel models, allowing customers to browse online and collect purchases in-store. Ultimately, physical spaces must deliver tactile engagement that digital interfaces cannot replicate.

While consumer choice should remain autonomous, I believe people bear a civic responsibility to patronize neighborhood stores. When consumers blindly prioritize the convenience of digital conglomerates, diverse high-street businesses collapse, leading to economic homogenization. Spending locally preserves artisan traditions and revitalizes community public spaces. Thus, conscious consumerism is not merely an economic decision, but an ethical investment in the vitality of one's own living environment.

p1: Yes, I really enjoyed science classes during secondary school because they included practical experiments. For instance, mixing chemical solutions in the laboratory made theoretical concepts instantly come alive and sparked my curiosity.

I am particularly fascinated by astronomy because exploring distant celestial bodies is awe-inspiring. Reading articles about the James Webb Space Telescope regularly keeps me updated on how our universe was originally formed.

Yes, I visited the national science museum in Hanoi last summer. It had fantastic interactive physics exhibits where visitors could test gravity and sound waves, which made learning incredibly engaging.

Definitely, because scientific literacy helps us make informed everyday choices regarding health and technology. For example, understanding basic hygiene and food preservation prevents foodborne illnesses in our daily cooking routine.

Generally speaking, yes, my neighborhood is quite secure with low crime rates. Neighbors look out for each other, and local security guards actively patrol the streets during night hours to deter theft.
I always double-check that all doors and balcony windows are securely locked before heading out. Additionally, I turn off main gas valves to avoid any potential domestic fires while away.
Yes, our primary school teachers regularly instructed us on basic road safety guidelines. They taught us how to use pedestrian crosswalks and always look both ways before crossing crowded streets.

Modern tech enhances our safety significantly through digital surveillance and emergency alerts. For instance, smartphone location-sharing features allow family members to track my commute and ensure I arrive home safely at night.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about the Mid-Autumn Festival, known locally as Tết Trung Thu, which is celebrated on the full moon night of the eighth lunar month. Last year, I spent the evening with my extended family and several neighborhood friends in my hometown. Leading up to the night, streets were vibrant with bright red lanterns and bustling stalls selling sweet mooncakes. During the festival, children paraded through the alleys carrying star-shaped lanterns while energetic lion dance troupes performed to the thumping beat of drums. My family gathered on our rooftop patio to share tea, taste baked lotus-seed mooncakes, and admire the luminous full moon. This celebration made a deep impression on me because it provided a rare moment of genuine connection amidst our hectic modern routines. In our fast-paced digital world, witnessing generations reconnecting over folklore stories, shared laughter, and traditional treats truly reaffirmed the warmth and enduring charm of Vietnamese cultural values.
p3: In my view, traditional festivals provide younger generations with a vital sense of belonging and cultural identity. Amid modern globalization, youth often search for roots, and festive rituals allow them to connect with ancestral history. For example, wearing traditional attire like the ao dai during New Year festivities fosters genuine communal pride. Thus, these events remain profoundly relevant despite technological shifts.

From my perspective, heavy commercialization tends to dilute the spiritual essence of cultural holidays. When retailers prioritize profit through aggressive marketing of gifts and luxury items, the core values of gratitude and family togetherness are frequently overshadowed. For instance, Mid-Autumn celebrations now emphasize extravagant packaging rather than moon viewing. Consequently, holidays risk turning into consumer-driven spectacles rather than heartfelt cultural traditions.

I firmly believe authorities play an indispensable role in safeguarding intangible heritage by funding cultural conservation and organizing authentic community events. Financial backing enables master artisans to train younger apprentices in ancestral arts. By contrast, without state support, folk singing or traditional craft demonstrations might vanish entirely due to lack of commercial profitability. Therefore, robust government patronage ensures that living cultural customs survive for posterity.

I completely agree that educational institutions ought to integrate traditional festivities into their curricula. Experiencing folklore through interactive school pageants helps students grasp historical values far better than passive textbook memorization. Whereas rote learning makes history abstract, making traditional food or participating in folk dances creates memorable cultural engagement. In short, school-based celebrations are crucial for cultivating cultural literacy and national pride in younger learners.

While Western events like Halloween or Christmas enjoy immense popularity among city youth, I do not believe they completely eclipse domestic heritage. International festivities are primarily perceived as fun entertainment, whereas native festivals retain profound familial and spiritual resonance. For example, youngsters might attend costume parties in October, but they always return home for Lunar New Year. Ultimately, global trends coexist with indigenous traditions rather than entirely replacing them.

p1: Yes, I have. During high school, I joined a local charity drive that distributed food packages to disadvantaged families in my hometown, which was a genuinely rewarding experience for me.
I believe people volunteer primarily to give back to society. Engaging in selfless work gives them a sense of purpose and helps them connect deeply with others in their local community.

Definitely, because it fosters empathy and civic responsibility early on. For example, my university required volunteer credits, which encouraged many students like me to care more about underprivileged groups.
In the future, I would love to teach basic English to children in remote mountainous regions, because quality education can open up transformative life opportunities for those underprivileged kids.
Yes, I had quite a large social circle back then. We lived in a close-knit neighbourhood, so I spent almost every afternoon playing tag and hide-and-seek with dozens of peers.
My favourite outdoor pastime was definitely riding bicycles around the village lake. My cousins and I would race until sunset, which was both exhilarating and great for our physical fitness.
Not necessarily. While modern kids have access to amazing digital entertainment, older generations enjoyed much more outdoor freedom and genuine face-to-face socialisation without screen addiction.
My happiest memory was going on summer road trips to the beach with my extended family. We would camp on the sand and cook fresh seafood together under the starry sky.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about Notion, an all-in-one productivity application that has completely transformed how I manage my everyday routine. I first discovered it about two years ago through a university classmate who was using it to take structured lecture notes and track group assignments. Essentially, Notion acts as a digital workspace where users can build customized databases, calendars, to-do lists, and personal planners. It offers versatile features like recurring reminders, kanban boards, and cloud synchronisation across my phone and laptop, allowing me to update my schedule seamlessly on the go. The primary reason this app is indispensable for organising my daily life is its extreme flexibility. Prior to using Notion, I constantly juggled sticky notes and multiple reminder apps, which often resulted in missed deadlines and clutter. Now, I have consolidated everything into one centralized dashboard, from my weekly grocery lists and study timetables to long-term financial budgets. Whenever a new task arises, I immediately log it into my schedule. This system keeps me focused, reduces mental fatigue, and ensures I never overlook critical responsibilities.
p3: Mobile applications have made time management far more streamlined and quantifiable than ever before. People can now schedule appointments, set automated reminders, and track their productivity metrics instantly. In contrast to paper planners, digital calendars alert users proactively about upcoming deadlines. While this creates unprecedented efficiency, it can also lead to hyper-scheduled lifestyles, which means people must actively balance digital convenience with spontaneous downtime.

Yes, over-reliance on digital tools can diminish certain cognitive faculties, particularly prospective memory and mental calculation. When individuals outsource routine mental tasks like remembering appointments or memorising phone numbers to software, their brain's natural recall abilities weaken. For example, many adults now struggle to recall simple schedules without checking their phones. Therefore, maintaining some mental effort without digital assistance is vital for long-term brain health.

The primary ethical issue is the invasion of personal privacy without explicit and informed consent. Many apps gather extensive personal routines, location logs, and financial records under the guise of customisation. While this enables tailored user experiences, these sensitive profiles are often monetised or vulnerable to data breaches. Consequently, governments must enforce stringent digital privacy laws to safeguard individual autonomy and protect consumer rights against corporate exploitation.

Artificial intelligence will likely transition productivity software from passive task trackers into proactive personal assistants. Instead of requiring users to input data manually, future tools will autonomously predict schedules, draft emails, and allocate resources based on past behavioural patterns. While this shift will drastically minimise human administrative burden, it might reduce human agency, making it essential that individuals maintain ultimate oversight over automated workflows.

Elderly citizens frequently struggle because they grew up in an analogue era without intuitive familiarity with touchscreen interfaces and digital conventions. Moreover, many modern apps feature complex navigation and small font sizes, creating physical barriers for seniors. In contrast, younger digital natives learn these systems organically from childhood. Thus, tech developers should prioritize accessible design and inclusive tutorials to prevent the digital marginalisation of older demographics.

p1: At the moment, I am working as a digital marketer for a tech startup. I really enjoy it because I get to design creative campaigns, such as launching social media ads for new software apps.

I believe adaptability and effective communication are crucial for career growth. In dynamic fields like business, professionals who quickly embrace changes and express ideas clearly tend to advance much faster than others.
Yes, I am actually planning to transition into project management within the next few years. That is why I am currently studying for professional certifications like Agile and PMP in my spare time.

I definitely prefer teamwork because pooling diverse perspectives usually leads to better solutions. For example, during complex assignments, collaborating with colleagues helps us solve bottlenecks much quicker than working alone.
I really love cool, breezy autumn weather. It is refreshing and comfortable for outdoor activities, like cycling around the local park or sitting outside at a cafe without sweating.
Definitely, especially during the heavy monsoon season. Torrential downpours often cause terrible traffic jams in my city, forcing me to leave home an hour earlier or work remotely instead.
I much prefer cold winter days to scorching summers. When it is chilly, I can simply put on a warm coat and enjoy hot soup, whereas extreme heat feels suffocating and draining.

Yes, summers seem to be getting significantly hotter and drier each year. For instance, last summer saw record-breaking heatwaves in northern regions, which disrupted daily life and pushed air-conditioning demand sky-high.
answers.sample: I would like to talk about a university project where my team designed a charity fundraising campaign during our final year. Our group consisted of four classmates from diverse backgrounds, including an aspiring graphic designer, a finance major, a research specialist, and myself. My primary role was project coordinator. I was responsible for scheduling weekly milestones, delegating tasks, and ensuring our messaging stayed aligned with the charity's mission. I also took the lead in pitching our concept to local community sponsors. Overall, this experience was both challenging and incredibly rewarding. The main difficulty lay in balancing our contrasting working styles and hectic schedules, as we were all juggling exams simultaneously. Misunderstandings occasionally cropped up regarding project deadlines. However, by establishing transparent communication channels on Slack and holding brief daily check-ins, we overcame these obstacles effectively. In the end, our initiative raised over two thousand dollars for an underprivileged children's shelter. It proved to be a resounding success, teaching me invaluable lessons about mutual accountability, conflict resolution, and the undeniable power of collaborative effort.
p3: In my view, active listening and emotional intelligence are the hallmarks of a great leader. Rather than merely dictating orders, an inspiring manager values diverse input and motivates subordinates according to their individual strengths. In contrast, authoritarian leaders often stifle innovation and breed workplace resentment. Therefore, true leadership is rooted in fostering psychological safety and empowering colleagues rather than asserting dominance.

I think personality clashes and an unwillingness to compromise are the primary culprits. Many individuals possess competitive mindsets, prioritizing personal recognition over shared objectives. For instance, perfectionists often struggle to delegate responsibilities because they lack trust in their teammates' competencies. Consequently, these behavioral tendencies create friction and disrupt productivity, preventing teams from realizing their collective potential unless interpersonal communication is improved.

Schools should prioritize teamwork while still acknowledging individual excellence. Although healthy competition can motivate pupils to surpass their personal limits, modern workplaces overwhelmingly demand interpersonal synergy and collaborative problem-solving. When institutions assign group projects instead of solely ranking students, children learn vital social skills like negotiation and empathy. Thus, cultivating a cooperative mindset prepares youth far better for future professional environments.

Technology has undeniably revolutionized collaboration by breaking down geographical barriers. Tools like Zoom and collaborative cloud platforms allow remote teams to coordinate seamlessly across international borders in real time. Nevertheless, virtual interactions can occasionally lack non-verbal cues and informal warmth, which sometimes leads to miscommunication. Overall, while digital tools maximize operational efficiency, groups must make deliberate efforts to maintain meaningful personal connections.

Generally speaking, smaller teams tend to be far more agile and productive. In oversized groups, communication becomes fragmented, and a phenomenon known as social loafing often occurs, where certain individuals contribute less. Conversely, compact groups of four to six members enjoy streamlined decision-making and clearer individual accountability. Hence, keeping team sizes relatively small usually maximizes output without sacrificing coherence or morale.
